title: Comparing Piston Flow and Dispersion Models for the Age of Groundwater Collected Through Very Short Screens
content:
Abstract

In previous groundwater dating studies involving samples collected through probes with very short screens, the tracer analysis has assumed the groundwater to have an age range so narrow that it can reasonably be considered a single age (a piston flow interpretation). We evaluated this assumption by re-examining age-dating tracer data from two previous studies in which groundwater was collected beneath coastal plain streams through screens 5 cm in length. Five age-dating tracer signals (SF6, 3H, 3Hetrit, 3H0, 3H/3H0) were fit to two lumped parameter models: the piston flow model (PFM), and the dispersion model (DM) which allows for a range of ages in a sample. At 38 of 40 sampling points, the PFM age was nearly identical to the DM mean age (median difference was <1 year), indicating the PFM and DM almost always agreed on the age of the samples. This held true whether the DM age distribution was narrow or wide, though most were narrow: ±1σ was within ±4 years at 29 of 40 sampling points, consistent with minimal effect of dispersion on the tracer-based ages. Results suggest the PFM is generally sufficient for interpreting groundwater age from tracer data in samples collected through very short screens, even beneath gaining streams where convergence of groundwater flowlines is expected. Although the PFM is typically sufficient for groundwater collected through very short screens, when multiple age-dating tracers are available the DM may provide additional insights on dispersion, ages, and chemical concentrations in groundwater.
